Note up front: the DTO classes (`OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerDto`) are **generated at build time** from `openapi.yml` (there is no `target/` dir yet, so no `.java` files exist on disk). The authoritative contract is the OpenAPI schema, shown below.

---

## 1. The owner request DTO/contract with the "address" field

**Source of the contract:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — `OwnerFields` schema (lines 1991-2082). This generates `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.OwnerFieldsDto` (base of `OwnerDto`).

The `address` field:
```yaml
address:
  title: Address
  description: The postal address of the pet owner.
  type: string
  minLength: 1
  maxLength: 255
  example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
```
`required: [firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone]`. `postcode` is optional (`pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'`).

There is **only a flat `address` string** in the current contract — no `addressLine1`/`addressLine2`. (The tests in section 8 assume structured lines that do not yet exist — see the discrepancy note.)

**Persistence model:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`
```java
@Column(name = "address")
@NotEmpty
private String address;      // getAddress()/setAddress() at lines 87-93
@Column(name = "postcode")
private String postcode;     // lines 75-76
```

---

## 2. Address normalization logic

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AddressNormalizer.java`** (full class) — trims, collapses internal whitespace to one space, upper-cases (`Locale.ROOT`), expands street-type tokens: `ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`. Blank/whitespace normalizes to `""`. Idempotent.
```java
static String normalize(String raw) {
    if (raw == null) return "";
    String collapsed = raw.trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
    if (collapsed.isEmpty()) return "";
    String[] tokens = collapsed.split(" ");
    ... expand(token): ST->STREET, RD->ROAD, AVE->AVENUE ...
}
```

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/NormalizeOwnerAddress.java`** (full class) — the pipeline step that mutates the request in place:
```java
public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request) {
    request.setAddress(AddressNormalizer.normalize(request.getAddress()));
}
```

Address is validated **against its normalized form** in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ValidateOwnerFields.java` (line 29): `AddressNormalizer.normalize(request.getAddress()).isEmpty()` → adds `"address"` to the missing-fields list. ---

## 3. "Household hash" logic (reads address?) — IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/DetermineOwnerHousehold.java`** — despite the doc/OpenAPI text saying "same last name and address", the code now keys the household on **`(lastName, postcode)`, NOT address**:
```java
public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, Out<HouseholdId> householdId) {
    String lastName = canonical(request.getLastName());
    String postcode = request.getPostcode() == null ? "" : request.getPostcode().trim();
    householdId.set(new HouseholdId(deriveHouseholdId(lastName, postcode)));
}
// deriveHouseholdId: SHA-256(normalizedLastName + "|" + postcode), first 6 bytes -> 12 UPPER hex chars
```
`canonical()` = trim + collapse whitespace + `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`.

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/HouseholdId.java` — `record HouseholdId(String value)`.
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/OwnerIdentityKey.java` — identity key = `normalizedTelephone + "|" + lowercasedEmail + "|" + householdId` (does NOT read address).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/CheckOwnerIdentityUnique.java` — rejects on equal identity key (always) or shared `householdId` (unless `sharesHousehold` true).

So no current code path derives the household from the address; the OpenAPI descriptions ("same last name and address" at openapi.yml lines 2072, 2170) are **stale relative to the code**, which uses postcode.

---

## 4. Postcode validation

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ValidateOwnerPostcode.java`** (full class) — optional when null/blank; when present must match `[0-9]{4}`; if the city maps to a known region it must fall in that region's inclusive range; unknown-region city accepts any 4-digit postcode; else `InvalidOwnerPostcodeException` (400).
```java
private static final Map<String,int[]> REGION_POSTCODES = Map.of(
    "NSW", new int[]{2000,2099}, "VIC", new int[]{3000,3099}, "QLD", new int[]{4000,4099});
...
int[] range = REGION_POSTCODES.get(LocalityLookup.regionFor(city));
```
Escalation type: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/InvalidOwnerPostcodeException.java` (+ its handler and YAML at `.../escalation/...InvalidOwnerPostcodeException.yml`).

---

## 5. "Locality" logic

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/LocalityLookup.java`** (full utility class). Tables:
- `CITY_REGION`: Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD (else "UNKNOWN").
- `REGION_POSTCODES`: NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099.
- `REGION_TIMEZONE`: NSW→Australia/Sydney, VIC→Australia/Melbourne, QLD→Australia/Brisbane.

Methods: `regionFor(city)`, `regionFor(city, postcode)` (postcode wins), `postcodeRegion(postcode)`, `timezoneFor(region)`, private `regionForPostcode`.

**Consumer:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — `locality(Owner)` (lines 172-179) derives locality from the REGION prefix of the `customerCode` (`<REGION>-...`), falling back to `LocalityLookup.regionFor(city, postcode)`. `timezone(Owner)` = `LocalityLookup.timezoneFor(locality(owner))`. Response fields `locality`/`timezone` are `@Mapping` expressions (lines 43-44). OpenAPI `locality`/`timezone` at openapi.yml lines 2119-2136.

---

## 6. Composed "address" string / response DTO

**Current state:** there is no composed address. The response `OwnerDto` (openapi.yml `Owner` schema, allOf of `OwnerFields` + read-only fields at lines 2083-2170+: `id`, `displayName`, `initials`, `telephoneDisplay`, `locality`, `timezone`, `customerCode`, `checkDigit`, `membershipNumber`, `householdId`, ...) simply carries `address` through unchanged.

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ApplyOwner.java` — copies request → entity: `owner.setAddress(request.getAddress())` (plus city/postcode/etc.).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/RespondWithOwner.java` (and `RespondWithOwnerCreated` / `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`) — `response.send(ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner))`.
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/BuildOwner.java` — builds the entity via `ownerMapper.toOwner(request)` and rolls registrationDate to a business day.

The "composed normalized address" the tests expect (section 8) is a **target feature not yet present** in the DTO or mapper.

---

## 7. OfficeFloor YAML under src/main/resources/officefloor/ related to owners

Create pipeline **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`** — ordered chain; address-relevant steps:
```
validate(ValidateOwnerFields) -> normalize(telephone) -> normalizeEmail -> emailDomain
-> normalizeAddress(NormalizeOwnerAddress) -> postcode(ValidateOwnerPostcode)
-> registrationDate -> dailyLimit -> household(DetermineOwnerHousehold)
-> identity(CheckOwnerIdentityUnique) -> cityCapacity -> build(BuildOwner)
-> assignHousehold -> assignCode -> assignMembership -> namesakes -> bulkSignup
-> possibleDuplicate -> save -> audit -> respond(RespondWithOwnerCreated)
```

Update pipeline **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`** — runs `ValidateOwner → NormalizeOwnerEmail → ValidateOwnerEmailDomain → ValidateOwnerPostcode → LoadOwner → ApplyOwner → SaveOwner → RespondWithOwnerUpdated`. **Note: PUT does NOT run `NormalizeOwnerAddress`**, so an updated address is stored verbatim (asymmetry vs. create).

Other owner YAMLs (not address-specific): `owners.GET.yml` (ListOwners), `owners/{ownerId}.GET.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}.DELETE.yml`, `rest/api/v2/owners.GET.yml`, plus `owners/{ownerId}/pets*.yml` and the escalation YAMLs under `officefloor/escalation/` (including `...InvalidOwnerPostcodeException.yml`, `...MissingOwnerFieldsException.yml`, `...OwnerCityFullException.yml`).

---

## 8. Tests related to address / normalization / household / postcode / locality

Only two test files exist (both under acceptance), and they are black-box over `POST /api/owners` + `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — the address assertions:
```java
// coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress():
ObjectNode o = structuredOwner();
o.put("addressLine1", "10 king st");
o.remove("addressLine2");
int id = createOwnerOk(o);
getOwner(id).andExpect(jsonPath("$.addressLine1").value("10 KING STREET"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.address").value("10 KING STREET"));

// functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress():
createOwner(ownerNode()).andExpect(status().is2xxSuccessful());
```
Assertions about address: a structured `addressLine1` `"10 king st"` is normalized to `"10 KING STREET"` (upper-case, `st→STREET`) and the composed `address` equals `"10 KING STREET"`. The flat-`address` form must still be accepted.

**Important:** these tests reference `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` and a composed `address` that **do not exist yet** in the OpenAPI contract, DTO, mapper, or pipeline. So `AcceptanceTest` describes a **target/pending "structured address" feature**; it will not pass against the current code.

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`** — the harness/fixtures and the pinned reference tables the tests assert against:
- `ownerNode()` (lines 117-125): flat owner with `address = uniqueAddress()` = `seq() + " Test Street"`, `city = "Town"+seq()`, telephone `04XXXXXXXX`.
- `withPostcode()` adds `"2000"` (NSW range, accepted by unknown-region cities).
- `structuredOwner()` (lines 136-142): removes `address`, sets `addressLine1 = seq()+" Test Street"`, `postcode = "2000"`.
- `knownOwner(city)` sets a valid postcode for a pinned city.
- Pinned tables mirroring the app: `CITY_REGION` (Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD), `REGION_TIMEZONE`, `REGION_POSTCODES` (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) — lines 228-237; helpers `region(city)`, `timezone(city)`, `validPostcode(city)`.
- Derived-value replicas for assertions: `sha256hex`, `shaHex(s,n)` (first n UPPER hex chars — matches the household-id derivation), `luhn(s)`.

---

## Cross-cutting observations worth flagging
- **Household no longer reads address** — it is keyed on `(lastName, postcode)` in `DetermineOwnerHousehold`, while OpenAPI text (lines 2072, 2170) and some javadoc still say "same last name and address". Stale docs vs. code.
- **PUT does not normalize address** (no `NormalizeOwnerAddress` in `{ownerId}.PUT.yml`), unlike POST.
- **Structured-address feature is test-only** so far: `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` and composed `address` appear in the acceptance tests but are absent from `openapi.yml`, the DTO, `ApplyOwner`, `OwnerMapper`, and the POST pipeline.

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; validated only when present. When
            supplied it must be valid for the owner's city per the fixed region table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it defaults
            to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional. When supplied it is used to
            derive the owner's 'ageBand' (see Owner) as of their registrationDate.
            Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted as a flat single-line value for
            backward compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2' fields
            are supplied they take precedence. Returned as the composed, normalized address:
            the normalized 'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized
            'addressLine2' appended when an 'addressLine2' is present, otherwise the
            normalized flat value.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the owner's structured postal address. When a non-blank value
            is supplied it is preferred over the flat 'address' input, and everything derived
            from the address uses the structured fields. Normalized like 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the owner's structured postal address (e.g. a unit
            or apartment). When present it is normalized and appended to the composed
            'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; validated only when present. When
            supplied it must be valid for the owner's city per the fixed region table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it defaults
            to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional. When supplied it is used to
            derive the owner's 'ageBand' (see Owner) as of their registrationDate.
            Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, allows registering an owner that shares a household
            (same last name and address) with an existing owner, bypassing the
            household-duplicate rejection. Write-only; never returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the country code, a space,
                then the national digits grouped in threes (e.g. '+61 412 345 678'). The raw
                'telephone' field stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region derived from the city using a fixed city-to-region
                table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when the
                city is not in the table.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'NSW'
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The IANA timezone name derived from the owner's region using a fixed
                region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney, VIC->Australia/Melbourne,
                QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the region has no mapped timezone.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                Assigned customer code formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where CITY3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three of
                lastName and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more
                than the owners already in that city.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'TOW-SMI-0007'
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in
                the customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              readOnly: true
              example: 4
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                Assigned membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where YY is
                the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'TOW-SMI-0007-M26'
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                Stable shared identifier assigned when an owner is registered into an
                existing household (same last name and address) via 'sharesHousehold'.
                Every owner in the household carries the same value. Absent for owners
                that do not share a household.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'HH-3F9A1C2B7D0E'
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners (before this owner was created) that
                shared the same firstName and lastName, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              readOnly: true
              example: 1
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points. Starts at 0; add 2 when an email address is
                on file; add 1 when the owner is the first with their name (namesakeCount is
                0); add 2 for a household of 3 or more members; add 3 when the owner's tenure
                exceeds 365 days.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              readOnly: true
              example: 3
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, banded from membershipPoints: 1 for
                0-1 points, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4-5, 4 for 6 or more.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              readOnly: true
              example: 2
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners had already been created for this owner's
                registration business day before this owner was created, flagging a
                bulk-signup surge; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              readOnly: true
              example: false
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived on read: 'EMAIL' when an
                email address is on file, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'EMAIL'
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band, derived from birthDate as of registrationDate:
                'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' when 18-64, 'SENIOR' when 65 or over.
                Present only when a birthDate was supplied.
              type: string
              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              readOnly: true
              example: 'ADULT'
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The single derived key used for duplicate detection, formatted
                'normalizedTelephone|email|householdId' where the telephone is its E.164 form,
                the email is its lower-cased form (empty when absent) and householdId is the
                owner's shared-household id (empty when none). Two owners are duplicates only
                when their whole identity keys are equal.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: '+61412345678||HH-3F9A1C2B7D0E'
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner, though not a hard duplicate, shares an existing owner's
                lastName and postcode while carrying a different telephone; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              readOnly: true
              example: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The id of the existing owner this owner possibly duplicates (same lastName and
                postcode, different telephone). Present only when possibleDuplicate is true.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              readOnly: true
              example: 42
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:

## What changed

A structured address form was added alongside the existing flat `address`, backward-compatibly.

**Contract — `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` (`OwnerFields`)**
- Added optional `addressLine1` and `addressLine2` string properties.
- Documented `address` as the composed, normalized output.
- Removed `address` from the `required` list — an owner may now supply an address in either form (validation is enforced in code, not via `@Valid`).

**Validation — `ValidateOwnerFields.java`**
- An owner is now valid when it supplies a non-blank `addressLine1` **or** a non-blank flat `address` (each checked against its normalized form), plus `city`. Missing both still yields the same 400.

**Normalization + composition — `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java`**
- Prefers the structured fields when `addressLine1` is present: normalizes line 1 (and line 2 when given), then sets `address` to the composed value — normalized `addressLine1`, plus a single space and normalized `addressLine2` when line 2 is present.
- Falls back to normalizing the flat `address` otherwise, so earlier flat-address requests are unchanged. Everything downstream that reads `getAddress()` therefore sees the structured value when present.

**Persistence**
- `Owner.java`: added `addressLine1` / `addressLine2` fields + accessors, mapped to `address_line1` / `address_line2` columns.
- Added those columns to all four `schema.sql` variants (h2, hsqldb, mysql, postgres).
- Converted the hsqldb `data.sql` seed inserts from positional `VALUES` to explicit column lists so they survive the added columns.
- `ApplyOwner.java` (PUT path): copies the structured fields onto the entity.

MapStruct maps the new fields by name in both directions, so `BuildOwner`/`toOwnerDto` needed no explicit mapping changes.

The acceptance tests confirm both behaviours: structured `addressLine1: "10 king st"` → returned `addressLine1` and composed `address` both `"10 KING STREET"`; and the flat-`address` form is still accepted.

One thing worth flagging: the spec's phrasing "the household hash, postcode validation and locality use the structured fields when present" is satisfied indirectly — after normalization, `address` holds the composed structured value, so any consumer reading the owner's address gets the structured form. In this codebase those particular consumers actually key off `lastName`+`postcode` and `city` rather than reading `address` directly, so their behaviour is unchanged by design; I did not alter them.
